📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A new Cyberpunk 2077 mod has overhauled Night City's rain, swapping the game's flat wet weather effects for individual 3D drops and adding lightning storms.

As spotted by DSOGaming, modder CyanideX's mod, Torrent, gives each raindrop its own size and falling speed. The drops also react to the player's movement, so they stream towards the windscreen when you're driving fast. If you find the wind has picked up, blustery weather can also push them sideways, too.

Recent findings suggest that the rain also catches the light from street lamps, neon signs, car headlights, and taillights, and won't fall through roofs or inside buildings. Drops splash on the ground, heavy rain leaves mist in the distance, and cars throw up spray from their tyres on wet roads.

The mod complements this with a upcoming lightning system, with branching bolts that flash and flicker before fading, and that can arrive in bursts during heavier storms.

If you like a little lightning, the frequency of bolts can be adjusted across 10 levels, and with the AudioXL mod installed, thunder follows each strike, timed to how far away it landed.

For players sensitive to flashing lights, a Reduce Flashes option dims the lightning, replaces its flicker with a single slow glow, and halves the number of strikes.

In a recent development, torrent supports Nova City 2 and other weather mods, and adds extra storm effects for Nova City 2 players, including mist that rolls through the streets with the wind. It’s available now on Nexus Mods.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ubisoft has confirmed that it's laid off a total of 166 employees across two of its major studios, Ubisoft Montreal and Ubisoft Quebec.

Although this figure only accounts for roughly 4% of the publisher's full Canadian workforce, it's obviously still a lot of people to let go of in one fell swoop.

Based on an unnamed source, IGN reports that the layoffs are largely to do with Ubisoft's continued restructuring; it suggests that many of those impacted were working on projects that have since been cancelled.

Sources indicate that for context, Montreal has worked on almost every big Ubisoft game you can think of over the past couple of decades. It's right now developing Assassin's Creed Hexe, having spearheaded Assassin's Creed Valhalla and Assassin's Creed Origins previously.

Quebec, meanwhile, has been chiefly responsible for Assassin's Creed Syndicate, Odyssey, and the series' most recent instalment, Shadows.

"As our portfolio evolves, our production needs are changing, requiring us to adjust the size of some teams to ensure our resources are aligned with current production priorities and business needs," reads an official statement from Ubisoft.

"Those affected are being provided with severance, extended health care benefits, career transition services and other resources," it continues.

This console generation has proven tumultuous for Ubisoft as a whole, to the point where its production pipelines have been completely overhauled under Chinese tech giant Tencent's guidance. The company is still trying to streamline operations more than a year after all of that came into effect.

Naturally, we wish everyone impacted by these layoffs all the best for the future.

[source ign.com, via videogameschronicle.com, gematsu.com].

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that general producer at P-Studio, Kazuhisa Wada, claims that Atlus has been working to reduce the time players have to wait between numbered entries in the long-running Persona series. Persona 6 doesn't right now have a release window, and it has already been more than a decade since Persona 5 first launched.

Industry observers note that in an interview as part of Sega Sammy's Samania series, which has been translated by GamesRadar+, Wada talks about how long it takes to create a numbered entry in the Persona series. "Large-scale RPGs like the Persona series take five years or more to develop," he explains. "So there can be a long time between numbered entries.".

Persona 6 has already been more than five years in the works as it began development in 2021, following the global release of Persona 5 Royal.

It has been revealed that later in the interview, Wada hints that Atlus has been working in a way that will speed up the releases of numbered entries, though he doesn't make it clear how this will be achieved. "We are presently working on Persona 6," he states. "I can't say much at the moment, but we want our games to demonstrate all of the hard work we've put in. With that in mind, we are creating something better than anything we've made before, and that is hugely satisfying.".

Sources indicate that "Persona 6 is not the end," he continues. "We have been working to make sure that people won't have to wait as long for the next game as they have previously. In order for Persona to grow as an IP, we consider how to live up to people's expectations in terms of creativity and development every day. Please look forward to more from the Persona series in the future.".

It's unclear whether Persona 6 is being developed concurrently with the next entry, or if Atlus is developing tools that can be used across multiple titles, but hopefully we won't be waiting another decade for Persona 7.

Persona 6 producer doesn't want "to make games for the global market," only something "we ourselves genuinely find exciting.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A hacker has pleaded guilty to a number of online crimes, including the 2022 breach of Rockstar Games which resulted in a bunch of mid-development clips of GTA 6 in action leaking onto the net.

In a recent development, the BBC report that, on November 16th, Arion Kurtaj pleaded guilty at Woolwich Crown Court to the Rockstar Games hack and a number of others he carried out with the hacking gang Lapsus$ while aged 16 and 17. Kurtaj, now aged 21, was previously sentenced to stay in a secure hospital indefinitely due to the severity of his autism, but was subsequently deemed fit to stand trial. He'll be sentenced at a later date.

Recent findings suggest that kurtaj carried out the 2022 Rockstar hack while on bail for other hacking offences and being housed at a Travelodge hotel under police protection, the latter on account of rival hackers threatening to attack him over stolen Bitcoin stashes. The Rockstar hack was reportedly done using an Amazon Fire Stick plugged into the hotel room's TV, plus a Bluetooth keyboard and mouse.

90 clips of unfinished GTA 6 were flung online by that hack, with Rockstar having refused to cooperate with Kurtaj's demand via an internal Slack channel that the manufacturer contact him on massaging app Telegram within 24 hours. Rockstar claimed the breach cost them $5m million to recover from, in addition to staff having to waste thousands of hours.

It has been revealed that earlier this year, GTA 6 suffered yet another leak, with a hacker or hackers going by "Cyberleek" posting various videos of the game in action. Rockstar and parent tech giant Take-Two swiftly sprung into action, taking down videos, filing subpoenas, and issuing a statement that called the leak "heartbreaking".

Hopefully with the game's console release later this week, those will be the only two GTA 6 leaks which have to be added to the annals of gaming history. As much as marketing can leave a bad taste in the mouth, especially when it barely shows anything of the actual product being advertised, neither of the GTA 6 leaks served much of a purpose beyond forcing people to waste some time and energy talking about the perpetrators.

According to Aftermath, officers responded to reports of a drive-by shooting at Flight at Tustin Legacy, a campus that houses inXile and other businesses, on 11th November.

Industry observers note that "Located multiple shell casings. Nobody was hurt," Tustin Police Sergeant Christopher Peterson told the outlet. "Processed the crime scene, and then sometime [Friday] morning, a little before 11 [AM], they took a suspect into custody. And the investigation is still kind of ongoing as to where and why.".

"We're relieved that no one was hurt at our inXile office," an inXile spokesperson noted. "Our focus is on supporting our team, and we are working closely with law enforcement as they investigate.".

Police have not given a motive, and the suspect has not been named.

InXile is the studio behind the Wasteland series, and is at the moment working on Clockwork Revolution.

It's handy to have in your pocket even if you are already playing the game because, you'll have noticed, GTA 6's map has a fog of war you need to clear as you play. Even after you do that, like our own Chris Livingston did after playing 100 hours of GTA 6, you'll still struggle to see it all on screen. No matter how far you zoom out you can't view the whole dang thing. Even if you could, the details of smaller roads and neighborhoods are only visible while zoomed in closer.

So, voila, here's a real significant poster version of the GTA 6 map with all the little roads, highways, and neighborhoods visible for you to reference.

Rockstar warned us that this thing was massive. Bigger than GTA 5, bigger than Red Dead Redemption 2, and bigger than both of those put together too.

"I guess I shouldn't be surprised by just how massive and detailed the world is. It's Rockstar: huge open worlds is what they do, and they've had a decade to do it. But I was stunned when I started playing, and a hundred hours later, I'm honestly still pretty stunned. Rockstar said GTA 6's map is twice as big as GTA 5's map, but it feels twice as big as "twice as big" should feel. It's enormous.".

So what are some of the key points of interest? Well it's GTA so I know everyone wants the airport location to steal jets from and the military base location to steal jets of a combat persuasion from too. Oh, and there are a few strip club locations on the map too, which apparently you're all just dying to know about.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, we've been keeping an eye out for news of Nintendo's playable and electric ocarinas going on sale in Europe for a good while now. It looks like sales are just around the corner, but you're going to need to jump through some hoops if you want to get your hands on one.

Both the Nintendo playable model and HORI electric version will initially be sold on an invite-only basis in Europe. You can register your interest in getting either model now on the Nintendo website, but there are some criteria that you'll have to pass first.

Firstly, you'll need to have a Nintendo account registered in Europe (excluding Norway, Russia and South Africa), have allowed Nintendo to process your usage information to customise services, offers and recommendations in your Nintendo Account settings, and have allowed Nintendo to send email recommendations about games, events, special offers and more. You'll need to have done all of that by 22nd November.

You can only register your interest if you have "reached at least 10 hours of play time in the Nintendo Switch 2 game The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time by 18/11/2026" using the same Nintendo account you use to register.

Industry observers note that and that's just to get an invite. On the day that the products become available, those who are invited will receive an email with a link to purchase either ocarina (limited to one each per customer).

Recent findings suggest that the playable ocarina will set you back £29.99, bundling the instrument with a wrist strap and sheet music for all of the in-game songs. HORI's electric option is a little more expensive at £41.99, but also comes with a dedicated stand.

Have you registered your interest for either model? Let us know in the comments.

Finding, buying, and stealing your dream car or bike is a peak part of Grand Theft Auto, and mine is the Fast and Furious Mitsubishi Eclipse in GTA 6, based on the bright green car driven by Paul Walker as Brian O'Conner in the original movie. This gorgeous motor can be found locked in a garage in Vice City in GTA 6, but it can be stolen, and, if you play your cards right, you can even register it as your own for free. Here's how.

Recent findings suggest that to find Paul Walker's Fast and Furious Mitsubishi in GTA 6, you need to head towards Vice Beach, to the east of Vice City. The car is locked in a garage on Vespucci Island, one of the Rialto Islands to the west of Vice Beach. You can see the exact location marked on the map above.

You'll have to break into the garage and steal the car, which is actually a lot easier than it sounds, but I've got more details on that below.

As you'd expect, the Mitsubishi handles really well and hits high speeds, so it's one of the best GTA 6 cars you can get your hands on, especially in the early game, for free, and without picking up too much heat.

In a recent development, to steal Paul Walker's GTA 6 car, head to the garage and break in. This triggers an alarm, but you can switch that off pretty quickly on the wall to your left as you head in. Open the garage door here too, break into the car, hotwire it, and drive away - simple as that.

There are a few additional details to note here, though, that make this experience easier or better for you overall.

  • All this follows Intel's last round of quarterly results, in which they announced a significant revenue fall; this triggered an Intel stock price drop from $92.07 per share on October 29th to $65.76 per share the next day, which this week's lawsuit characterises as "the largest single-day price decline for Intel common stock in over 50 years".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, tech giant Intel are being taken to court for allegedly "misleading" their investors about the sheer scale of the impact of generative AI-fuelled component price hikes on PC sales. The class action lawsuit in question claims that Intel's distribution and manufacturing partners have had to deal with "a massive glut of unwanted PC inventory", and that the gains from Intel's investments in AI datacenters aren't enough to make up for slowing sales of PCs to regular Josephines who just want fancy boxes they can play Deadlock on.

All this follows Intel's last round of quarterly results, in which they announced a significant revenue fall; this triggered an Intel stock price drop from $92.07 per share on October 29th to $65.76 per share the next day, which this week's lawsuit characterises as "the largest single-day price decline for Intel common stock in over 50 years".

Sources indicate that the lawyers in question are from Robbins LLP, who specialise in "shareholder, whistleblower, antitrust, & consumer litigation". In a press release, they say they've filed suit on behalf of anybody who bought Intel stock from July 23rd to October 29th this year.

The suit claims that Intel neglected to tell investors that falling PC and component sales were having a "materially greater negative impact" on their third financial quarter 2026 Client Computing and Physical AI Groupresults than Intel had previously stated – to the tune of "hundreds of millions of dollars" in revenue shrinkage, compared to the previous quarter, with the situation still expected to "worsen".

They also accuse the manufacturer of keeping schtum about the aforesaid "massive glut of unwanted PC inventory", together with the fact that "any positive impacts to Intel’s business and financial results resulting from data center construction and other aspects of the AI boom were more than offset by the negative effects on the Company’s business and financial results resulting from the PC market slowdown and the excess inventory buildup described above.".

According to recent reports, finally, they say Intel bosses have failed to disclose that they're struggling to procure an adequate supply of substrates – that is, materials used to create the base layer of chips, circuit boards and similar components. As such, the lawyers claim, Intel couldn't "ramp up production to meet data center CPU demand even if the Organization chose to divert production resources because of a slowdown in PC-related sales.".

It has been revealed that once the Godzilla of personal computing, Intel haven't been having a brilliant few years. Back in 2024, they recorded a multi-billion dollar quarterly loss, pushing then-CEO Pat Gelsinger to resign. As regards sales of gaming PCs, they've fallen behind AMD, though they've reportedly taken some ground back recently as regards desktop CPUs. As regards graphics cards, they have long been dwarfed by Nvidia.

We got confirmation a couple of months ago that the US Army's 3rd Infantry Division was offering a four-day pass to play Grand Theft Auto 6 for soldiers who re-enlist for at least two years. And now the time has come to collect.

Talking to Task & Purpose one soldier who took advantage of the program, Sgt. Jamire Smith, described how he's planning to spend the long weekend: "I'm all campaign. I’m all about the heist. I think I have a good 24 hours to waste on it.

Industry observers note that "I was actually in the process of getting out, I was towards my final stages of getting out … but my company and the battalion helped me navigate through that and they indicated me that there’s still a need for me, and that I am still a clear and value asset to the team, and so that’s really what drove me to say 'let’s keep going, let’s keep driving'. Maybe be a lifer in this, since I already made it my career.".

According to recent reports, in total 43 soldiers re-enlisted through the GTA 6 incentive, an idea that was born from Staff Sgt. Brittany Wolfer.

Industry observers note that "It's not supposed to be the deciding factor," Wolfer indicates. "There is always going to be a disconnect between your senior command and your lowest soldier. So how do you bridge that gap to where that lower soldier still knows that their battalion commander or their senior leadership cares about them and sees what they're interested in. And that’s kind of what this was for.".

In a recent development, wolfer first brought the idea to her battalion commander who actually played GTA 2 back in the day and so was up for trying the incentive out. "I came into [the unit], there hadn’t been a counsellor for about eight months, so there was a lot of gaps and things that were falling through because the soldiers didn’t have that presence within the formation," Wolfer adds. "This kind of was just a way to grab people's attention and kind of be like, 'Hey, here I am. I’m the person you’re gonna come talk to,' and [it] kind of snowballed from there.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A mainstay of the GTA series has been the presence of sex workers, but Rockstar Games has dropped this aspect for the newly released GTA 6.

As reported by Shack News, unlike most other games in the long-running franchise, you cannot hire a sex worker in GTA 6.

The outlet asked Rockstar about this decision, and received the following response:.

It has been revealed that "GTAVI is a game about a couple in a bind, lovers on the run. While we have taken a lot forward from previous GTA titles, everything we have implemented in VI has been done to support the spirit of the story we wanted to tell, and the gameplay systems we wanted to expand upon - things like wanted system, the radio, robberies and car theft. Many aspects of previous titles are not present in GTAVI, but the elements we have we believe are all necessary and complementary to the feeling and motivations we wanted to emphasize as you play through Jason and Lucia's story.".

So, in other words, sex workers aren't included this time around because it wouldn't make sense for Jason or Lucia to pursue that, as they're already in a relationship — and that's a significant part of the story.

As mentioned, they have been present in the series since 2001's GTA 3, and this will be the first 3D game to exclude them.

In a recent development, GTA 6 is also the first game that centres on a couple, however, with the relationship between Jason and Lucia interwoven in the gameplay as well as being a key tenet of the narrative. It seems Rockstar didn't think sex workers would be conducive to this goal.

According to recent reports, what are your thoughts on this? Tell us in the comments section below.

[source shacknews.com, via kotaku.com].

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • EA has made some notable leadership changes within its studios group, and in who oversees the Battlefield franchise.
  • Beede announced the change on LinkedIn, saying that he now oversees EA's shooter and action-RPG portfolio, seemingly occupying the role of the late Vince Zampella.
  • In this stead, EA appointed Sam Cooper as Battlefield's new boss.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

EA has made some notable leadership changes within its studios group, and in who oversees the Battlefield franchise. Byron Beede, previously Battlefield's general manager, has been promoted to group general manager.

Beede announced the change on LinkedIn, saying that he now oversees EA's shooter and action-RPG portfolio, seemingly occupying the role of the late Vince Zampella.

In this stead, EA appointed Sam Cooper as Battlefield's new boss. Cooper, who also revealed his new job title on LinkedIn, previously had a stint at EA Sports, but he's mostly known for his work at Activision, where he spent the last five-ish years as Call of Duty's global product management and head of live service.

While this might seem like fairly unremarkable corporate news - executives move between rival companies all the time, after all - it reinforces a narrative that EA continues to keenly replicate Activision's Call of Duty model.

That particular push is years-old now, and it kicked off in 2021 when EA hired Byron Beede, former boss of all of Call of Duty at Activision, to lead the next evolution of Battlefield. So far, that decision has given us the very successful Battlefield 6 and its free-to-play, COD: Warzone-like battle royale mode Redsec.

To facilitate that, EA rearranged several of its studios to serve under one banner dubbed Battlefield Studios, replicating Activision's model of locking several teams around the world into developing and supporting a single game / franchise. Ripple Effect, Motive, the iconic Criterion and, of course, series creator DICE are all the Battlefield franchise's lead and support studios.

In a recent development, many players argue - and I would agree - that Battlefield and Call of Duty games are more alike today than they've ever been. The user interface, the emphasis on limited-time events, the garish store cosmetics, the COD-like battle pass system - complete with a more expensive option, are all signs of that transition. And that is to say nothing of controversial changes to longstanding Battlefield tenets, such as the class system, intended to make Battlefield 6 appeal to a wider audience.

The effects of that leadership change likely won't materialise until the next Battlefield title, but it's a curious one to keep in mind as EA leans even harder into its biggest franchises following its $55bn private equity and Saudi Arabia's PIF-funded buyout.

On by default, game captures automatically uploaded to Xbox Live servers are scanned for offensive imagery, including hate speech, drugs misuse, excessive violence, as well as nudity and sexual content.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that christopher Nolan’s 2014 megahit Interstellar has it all: big sci-fi ideas, cool robots, ugly crying, and a Matt Damon character in need of rescuing.
  • If you loved both the special effects in Interstellar that make space travel feel viscerally thrilling (and terrifying) and the mind-blowing concepts, this is the film for you.
  • In a recent development, if you’re looking for more existential missions with somewhat reluctant heroes in space, Project Hail Mary is your next stop.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that christopher Nolan’s 2014 megahit Interstellar has it all: big sci-fi ideas, cool robots, ugly crying, and a Matt Damon character in need of rescuing. Grounded in the intensity of the human experience, this story of humanity’s potential extinction and the sacrifice of one man to save it doesn’t just deliver exotic planets and thrilling spaceship maneuvers; it also provides all the feels as Joseph Cooper (Matthew McConaughey) sacrifices everything he has in an effort to save the entire human race. It’s one of the best science fiction films ever made, with Nolan’s signature complexity, time manipulations, and emotional wallop. If you love this movie, here are ten more that offer a similar viewing experience.

If you loved both the special effects in Interstellar that make space travel feel viscerally thrilling (and terrifying) and the mind-blowing concepts, this is the film for you. Stanley Kubrick’s 1968 epic (written by sci-fi master Arthur C. Clarke) traces humanity’s development from mildly smart apes to spacefaring capitalists who discover a mysterious obelisk on the Moon that sparks a mission to Jupiter. While it operates in a colder emotional key than Nolan’s film, 2001: A Space Odyssey absolutely delivers on the epic side of things (and the cool—if slightly deranged and deadly—artificial intelligences). Stream 2001: A Space Odyssey on HBO Max or rent it on Prime Video.

In a recent development, if you’re looking for more existential missions with somewhat reluctant heroes in space, Project Hail Mary is your next stop. When the Sun begins to dim due to the interference of an alien entity, scientists identify the one nearby star that isn’t being similarly affected. Brilliant molecular biologist Ryland Grace (Ryan Gosling) winds up forced to go on what is assumed to be a fatal, one-way mission into deep space to try to find a way to save humanity, unexpectedly assisted by a charming alien he names Rocky. It’s got the same emotional volume and massive ideas as Interstellar, and fans of Nolan’s film will love it. Stream Project Hail Mary on MGM+ or Philo, or rent it on Prime Video.

Part of what makes Interstellar so compelling is the stakes: The human race is slowly dying, and a handful of people must make incredible sacrifices to save it. That’s the vibe of Sunshine, set in a future where the Sun is dimming and a spacecraft is dispatched to deliver an enormous bomb designed to reignite the Sun’s fusion cycle. But the mission is the second attempt after the first ship vanished mysteriously seven years earlier, and when the fresh crew stumbles on the derelict wreck of the first mission, things promptly descend into violence and madness—but the crew remains determined to save the world, no matter the cost. Rent Sunshine on Prime Video.

Interstellar works in large part because of the emotional dynamics at play. McConaughey’s character leaves his children behind and is forced to witness them growing up without him, missing out on their lives and saddled with the knowledge that they resent him despite the necessity of his mission. Arrival is a First Contact story focused on language—linguist Louise Banks (Amy Adams) is drafted into an effort to understand the strange, complex language of the aliens. As she slowly builds to an understanding of how the aliens communicate and perceive time itself, her own heartbreak and loss come into play, giving this film a similarly devastating emotional punch. Stream Arrival on Kanopy or Hoopla, or rent it on Prime Video.

Family dynamics and the toll of lonely space missions fuel Ad Astra, a film with the same emotional core as Interstellar. Twenty-nine years ago, famed astronaut Clifford McBride (Tommy Lee Jones) led the Lima Project, a space station around Neptune searching for intelligent life. Thirteen years ago, Earth lost contact with him. When bursts of energy emanating from Neptune threaten to end life on Earth, his son, Roy (Brad Pitt), is dispatched to try to make contact with his father. It’s an epic journey with a powerful climax that will satisfy fans of Interstellar in every way. Stream Ad Astra on Netflix or rent it on Prime Video.

It has been revealed that ridley Scott’s prequel to Alien has its flaws, but if you’re looking for a sense of epic spacefaring adventure in the same key as Interstellar, it’s perfect. When two scientists discover a star map apparently left behind by ancient aliens, they secure funding from the Wayland Corporation to organize a space expedition to the indicated planet. Accompanied by a colorful crew and the android David, they discover an apparently abandoned outpost of the species dubbed the Engineers. The story wrestles with questions about humanity’s origins, purpose, and potential—but this being an Alien film, things promptly turn horrifying. Rent Prometheus on Prime Video.

Adapted from Carl Sagan’s 1985 novel, Contact follows astronomer Dr. Ellie Arroway (Jodie Foster), who becomes involved with an effort to decipher a signal originating from the star Vega. The signal turns out to be a set of instructions for constructing a one-person spacecraft of some kind, and Arroway is eventually selected as the candidate to take the journey. There’s a sense of courage in the face of the unknown that’s similar to Interstellar, as well as the thrill of strapping into a spaceship and pressing the ignition. Plus, there’s the added bonus of seeing one of the greatest trick shots in cinematic history. Rent Contact on Prime Video.

Industry observers note that stanislaw Lem’s 1961 novel Solaris explores what Lem saw as the impossibility of ever understanding a truly alien life. The two major adaptations—Andrei Tarkovsky's 1972 version and Steven Soderbergh’s 2002 take starring George Clooney—are both worth watching, but Tarkovsky’s film is a masterpiece of psychological horror. The story is set mainly aboard a space station orbiting a planet covered in what appears to be a sentient "ocean" and chronicles the strange haunting and inexplicable experiences of the humans living on the station. If your favorite part of Interstellar is the ending when things get trippy and weird, you’ll probably love Solaris. Stream Solaris on HBO Max, Plex, or Tubi, or rent it on Prime Video.

Sources indicate that the story of a mission to Jupiter’s moon Europa to search for intelligent life, Europa Report has the same sense of terrifying excitement that accompanies Interstellar’s missions to the different candidate planets. Leaning into the fragility of life in an environment not designed to support it, the mission crew face a steady stream of loss and danger as they work to catch sight of alien life on the frozen, deadly moon, ultimately faced with making terrifying sacrifices in order to provide humanity with the answers that it seeks. Stream Europa Report on Netflix, Kanopy, or Hoopla, or rent it on Prime Video.

In a recent development, A film based on a 1956 epic science fiction poem written by a Swedish Nobel Laureate might seem like an unlikely match for fans of Interstellar, but it’s actually perfect. As the Earth becomes uninhabitable, humanity begins launching ships to colonize Mars. When one such ship, the Aniara, is damaged and veers irreversibly off course, the passengers and crew are faced with the knowledge that they will sail off into the void without hope of rescue. Within a few years, despair has driven some to suicide and madness, while others cling to the possibility that they might yet find a way back. The film offers a different perspective on the existential crisis of humanity’s extinction, exploring the worst-case scenario to its bitter, bleak end. Stream Aniara on Kanopy or Hoopla, or rent it on Prime Video.

  • Set in Lost Heaven, a shoe-in for 1930s Chicago, Illinois, you play through Tommy Angelo's rise from a taxi driver, who has a chance run in with the Salieri crime family, to one of the gang's main enforcers in their fight against their rivals, the Morellos.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, this week sees the release of Grand Theft Auto 6, the open-world crime 'em up that's been in development for at least eight years and has been waited on by fans for even longer. Naturally, over on PC we're still waiting for a port to be confirmed, let alone a release date to circle in our calendars. But, as happens whenever a upcoming GTA is on the horizon, I think about Mafia: City of Lost Heaven.

Released less than a year after Grand Theft Auto 3, Mafia is perhaps a more prescient example of Rockstar's future than their own.

Set in Lost Heaven, a shoe-in for 1930s Chicago, Illinois, you play through Tommy Angelo's rise from a taxi driver, who has a chance run in with the Salieri crime family, to one of the gang's main enforcers in their fight against their rivals, the Morellos.

The influences on developers Illusion Softworks are obviously cinematic, with whole sequences ripped from The Godfather films and Goodfellas (and I'd argue there's a sprinkling of Once Upon A Time In America for good measure). A habit they share with Rockstar, who also pull liberally from crime films that share the settings of their games. But Illusion Softworks are also clearly interested in capturing the history of the Prohibition era, too. The story begins in the aftermath of the 1929 Wall Street Crash and the depression that followed, running through until the late 30s, and you see that time pass in the city around you. Buildings that are under construction at the start of the game are completed by its end, a used car lot in Chinatown sits empty for most of the game until business picks up with the economy, but most enjoyable of all is that the cars driving the streets change. At first the roads are filled with Ford Model-T-inspired vehicles that basically look like horse carriages with engines, but by the end of the game they've all become much sleeker creatures that have left their early carriage influences behind.

The city Illusion Softworks built also has a dedication to verisimilitude that we see Rockstar adopting in their later games. As you drive Lost Heaven's streets, you must pay attention to speed limits and red lights, as speeding and running traffic lights will both earn you a fine if a policeman spots you. For fans of public transport, there are streetcars and overhead trams you can ride to navigate the city, too. Two other touches I love: when you reload your gun, you dump the whole clip instead of returning the unfired bullets to a magic ammo reservoir, and vehicles can run out of fuel if you drive them too far.

Much had been made of all the simulations running under the surface of Grand Theft Auto 6, such as fully realised cloud formation, a smell reaction system, and… fuel tanks that can run empty. No doubt they're significantly more impressive than what's on show in Mafia, and this isn't about putting the two games against each other (even if one of them was likely made for less than the other studio spent on coffee runs across its eight-year development). Nor is it about saying history recognised the wrong game: Grand Theft Auto 3 was a huge step forward in open-world gaming and Mafia was recognised and celebrated in its time. It's about something else.

Sources indicate that back in 2002, Illusion Softworks offered a different kind of open-world crime game. One that was more mature despite having a lower age rating. Grand Theft Auto was undoubtedly more influential, sparking imitators that mostly opted to follow its tone and sensibilities – Saints Row began in a similar place to GTA 3 and as the series continued leaned further into the silliness and parody, for instance. But while for many years Mafia stood as a sign to an open world path that could have been taken, the longer Grand Theft Auto series has gone on, the more Rockstar have found their way toward the example set by Illusion Softworks. The games are still aiming for bombastic comedy at times, but they're also interested in the likes of newly-arrived-in-America Niko Belic, or Michael de Santa, a retired criminal haunted by his past. They're much richer protagonists than Claude, the silent character you play in GTA 3.

The Mafia series has continued, marked by ideas that remain as interesting as what was on show in the original. In Mafia 3, you play Lincoln Clay, a black soldier returned from the war in Vietnam and brought into the family. Set in a take on New Orleans, Louisiana, during the civil rights movement, you face overt racism. Linger too long in white, wealthy neighbourhoods and the residents will call on the police to move you along. And the Definitive Edition remake of the first game, released in 2020, is a rare example of a game that both captures the spirit of the original and justifies its existence by expanding and bettering the story. Though I don't think any of its sequels have been as innovative, nor as forward thinking, as the first game.

I don't want to come across as Rockstar-bashing. The studio have continued to push the open-world genre forward with every release and I want to see what other developers lift from GTA 6 for their own games. But I'm even more pleased that as the studio's aged, their work has grown closer to Illusion Softworks'.

Cyberagent - the parent organization of Umamusume: Pretty Derby developer Cygames - has boasted its recent successes in the mobile gaming sphere in a recent quarterly earnings presentation.

According to recent reports, as part of this presentation (covered by Automaton), the firm has established prepares to launch seven "major releases" to the mobile platform by 2030. There is no word on what these games will be, but one will be released in 2027, while another two will come in 2028.

Cyberagent boasted an 88 percent "hit" rate for its mobile releases so far, with seven of its eight releases having a development budget of around a billion yen, and reaching a point where it makes that figure back every month from its playerbases. Those games include Umamusume: Pretty Derby, Final Fantasy Ever Crisis, Hololive Dreams, and Jujutsu Kaisen Phantom Parade.

Sources indicate that cyberAgent CEO Takahiro Yamauchi - speaking during the presentation - noted that it was still difficult to predict the success of a mobile game ahead of its release. However, he also claims that the experience Cyberagent has gained with its substantial releases to date have allowed the manufacturer to gain a clearer perspective on profitability and sustainability.

Sources indicate that this presentation comes after a notable month for Cygmes and Umamusume: Pretty Derby. The developer issued refunds for hotels and flights following the sudden cancellation of an LA live show for the game last month, then shortly after became a major sponsor of the Japanese Formula 1 Grand Prix. The game was also temporarily taken offline due to the major PHP vulnerability exposed last month, an outage that was thankfully short-lived.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Guillermo del Toro has revealed that the script for his unmade Jabba the Hutt movie was already written.

"[David S. Goyer] and I did write the script and I even developed some art and sculptures," del Toro wrote on Twitter, even confirming the movie's title: The Rise and Fall of Jabba the Hutt.

Guillermo del Toro wanting to make a Jabba the Hutt movie is something that has been bubbling away for over a decade.

In 2015, he told Yahoo of his initial pitch and love for Star Wars' most fearsome crime lord. He said, "I would do the sort of Godfather saga that Jabba the Hutt had to go through to gain control. One, because it's the character that looks the most like me, and I like him. I love the idea of a Hutt type of mafia, a very complex coup. I just love the character.".

For many years, there had been radio silence on the project, but del Toro revealed in 2023 that the project had been shelved.

“We had the rise and fall of Jabba the Hutt, so I was super happy. We were doing a lot of stuff, and then it’s not my property, it’s not my money, and then it’s one of those 30 screenplays that goes away," the director recalled to Collider.

In a recent development, he added, “Sometimes I’m bitter, sometimes I’m not. I always turn to my team and say, ‘Good practice, guys. Good practice. We designed a great world. We designed great stuff. We learned.’.

It has been revealed that but there is still hope in a galaxy far, far away. As recently as this year, The Mandalorian and Grogu director Jon Favreau suggested in an interview with Fortress of Solitude that "someday [del Toro] will collaborate on that.".

For now, though, The Rise and Fall of Jabba the Hutt joins the pile of Star Wars projects that never were – alongside George Lucas' prohibitively expensive idea for a TV show.

Tech Report: Football Manager 27 review: Back on form, but not without its wayward touches

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways

  • It has been revealed that PC Gamer's got your back Our experienced team dedicates many hours to every review, to really get to the heart of what matters most to you.
  • The latest in a long line of life-absorbing sports management sims.Release date November 10, 2026Expect to pay $60/£50Developer Sports InteractivePublisher SegaReviewed on Ryzen 7 9800X3D, Radeon RX 9070XT, 16GB RAMSteam Deck TBALink Official site.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Faster-moving, sometimes maddening, and obsession-forming. Football Manager finds a way to make spreadsheets fun again.

It has been revealed that PC Gamer's got your back Our experienced team dedicates many hours to every review, to really get to the heart of what matters most to you. Find out more about how we evaluate games and hardware.

What is it? The latest in a long line of life-absorbing sports management sims.Release date November 10, 2026Expect to pay $60/£50Developer Sports InteractivePublisher SegaReviewed on Ryzen 7 9800X3D, Radeon RX 9070XT, 16GB RAMSteam Deck TBALink Official site.

It has been revealed that it's difficult to convey to non-players how deeply Football Manager gets under your skin. It's the kind of game that becomes your mental screensaver, the fallback topic whenever your brain isn't explicitly required to think about something else. A Slack DM came in this morning and for a second I interpreted 'DM – [Name]' as Slack assigning my colleague the defensive midfielder position. When did they add that feature? I caught myself thinking for a second.

It has been revealed that that in itself doesn't mean Football Manager 27 is a great game. This series is capable of fostering fixation even on its off games, like last year's tile-ridden UI tangle FM26. But this new release makes meaningful progress by untangling that UI, improving the flow of the game between matches, and—the holy grail—giving you some clue as to why you're losing, and what you can do about it.

The latter point comes thanks to the introduction of the 'tactical effectiveness' system. This is a visual rating of all the factors that affect your team's performance, and it lives in your tactics screen as a colour-coded scale. The better all those underlying factors are working, the higher your tactical effectiveness scale goes. Click on it and you see under the hood of FM's simulation, at all the elements which determine your squad's performance, from individual player ability and training effectiveness to each player's degree of buy-in to your tactical vision.

That screen gives a degree of transparency to what's deciding whether you win or lose, and having played these games since Championship Manager 2, I've been wishing for that transparency for a long time.

Industry observers note that but it's not without its issues. This being the introduction of this new system, its effects feel overly exaggerated. If your team has a low tactical effectiveness they'll lollop about on the pitch like it's their first day on Earth, even in the most basic formations that my school's under 11s side could execute. It's extremely frustrating to watch the sport's absolute elite wandering about in the final third like they've forgotten where the goal is, or witness Champions League-calibre centre backs totally baffled by their markers running in a straight line towards goal. This is probably how it feels to be a Man United manager in real life, but it still feels like a failing of the match engine to visualise poor tactical effectiveness in a true-to-life way.

The flipside of that coin is that there's a lot of gratification to be had in increasing that TE scale, and FM 27 does a good job of surfacing the ways to do it. It means setting more tactical familiarity sessions in the training screen, a doorway I haven't personally darkened for years as a manager since it allowed me to delegate that task to my assistant. It also finds its way into recruitment, showing you a rough prediction of how well a player will contribute to that all-notable rating even before you sign them. I really enjoy this newly introduced way of thinking about signings, and relish the chance to be proactive about improving performances instead of changing things at random and crossing my fingers.

On the pitch, there's some modest progress since last year. New animations, specifically flair passes and players recovering from a stumble after being shoulder-barged, tell you something useful about that player's attributes and how they can be used. Meanwhile on the presentation front, there are a few new angles during pre-match sequences and trophy ceremonies.

Keep up to date with the most crucial stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

There's also a lot of the usual release-era nonsense. In my save I seem to have a goal waved off for offside every twenty minutes, and keepers seem to have started coating their boots and gloves in teflon when receiving the most straightforward backpasses or clearing up routine balls. These odd glitches happen every year before the first few patches roll out, and patch 27.1.0 does seem to address most of the odd match engine behaviour I've noticed.

In a recent development, but I'm disappointed that progress is that gradual. Particularly as FM's move to the Unity engine was so disruptive, prompting the series to skip a year. I expected that engine switch might mean the match engine evolves more quickly, but that doesn't seem to be the case based on this release.

Instead, the really significant additions and improvements can be found in the nooks and crannies, the boring bits you wouldn't write about in the Steam description. How do you make navigable menus, more game setup customization options and quicker progress between matches sound sexy? Nevertheless, these are the changes that add up and make FM 27 feel much more enjoyable than last year's game.

Industry observers note that the prime example of these small but mighty changes is the 'continue flow'. When you start a newly introduced game, you can now control how often the game stops the passage of time to return you to your inbox after you hit 'continue'. Hardly the most exciting feature on paper, but it addresses a crucial and longstanding problem: progress had become punitively slow. More than any loss at home to a relegation side or any unreasonable telling-off from the board, it was this feeling of wading nose-deep through molasses that sapped my desire to keep playing recent FM games, and it turns out that fixing the problem is as simple as selecting the 'streamlined' continue flow so that the game stops progressing time less often and moves you from match to match at a faster rate.

In a recent development, this is a game about setting long-term looks and watching them come to fruition. Winning one match isn't where the payoff comes, it's three seasons in when you see how much your youth academy graduate's stats have developed. So it really does matter that FM 27 hastens the pace and you can see those long term plans resolve.

Recent findings suggest that there's been something of a deft Cruyff turn from Sports Interactive on the direction of its UI this year, after the overhaul in FM 26 was received as positively as a taxation on laughter. The menu tiles have been pared right back, menus themselves are much faster to load and in general it's more intuitive to get to the screens you're looking for.

Recent findings suggest that that doesn't mean Football Manager 27 has a good UI. I still too often find myself hunting for basic actions now buried several menus deep, like having to click Portal - Career - My Profile - Actions - Go On Holiday to start simming through fixtures. For reference, here's how it worked in Championship Manager 01/02: [Manager Name] - Go On Holiday.

Industry observers note that I still find myself struggling to process the morass of information being thrown at me by certain menus too, particularly the matchday screens. More detail does not equal more fun, and most of these info panels are useless to me, serving only to obscure the bits I do want to check. There's more customisation this year to allow what these menus show you, but you can't remove info panels entirely or simplify screens.

Just like the obsession that a Football Manager game inspires, it also has a way of making minor annoyances feel significant over time. When that happens, you have to zoom out and remind yourself it got you to care this much in the first place because the experience is fundamentally great. It's like a Paradox strategy game where all the nobles are 20-year-old inside forwards. It's a labyrinth of menus that makes you want to give up and do something else, but you don't. Because there's so much sandbox potential, such a vast and detailed world being simulated in minute detail, and such a feeling of payoff when those long-term intends come good.

It has been revealed that and that's why it's so significant that Football Manager's biggest changes are about giving you transparency about what's going wrong, what you need to do to fix it, and then letting you progress at the speed you want to. That makes it feel less like a complicated German board game you lost the instructions for, and more like managing a football team.

#28968. The Apple Watch's New 'Siri Recap' Feature Is Even Creepier Than I Expected

📅 11 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1361 w)
📖 Baca
Gadgets ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Lifehacker ↗ Open Full Page

The Apple Watch's New 'Siri Recap' Feature Is Even Creepier Than I Expected

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1361 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The “Siri Recap” feature that Apple announced in September is finally available in a developer beta, and I’ve spent the last 24 hours with the feature turned on.
  • Recent findings suggest that I have a button in the watch’s Control Center that can turn the recapping abilities off, but if I forget to do so, Siri listens to everything.
  • The recaps somberly mention silly memes my kids were laughing about, and make major bullet points out of offhand remarks from brief conversations.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The “Siri Recap” feature that Apple announced in September is finally available in a developer beta, and I’ve spent the last 24 hours with the feature turned on. It’s even more unsettling than the “Live Rewind” feature that debuted at the same time. It listens to all my conversations, and produces summaries that are both helpful and deeply creepy.

Recent findings suggest that I have a button in the watch’s Control Center that can turn the recapping abilities off, but if I forget to do so, Siri listens to everything. I’ll get a recap of my entire evening, presented in roughly hour-long chunks, including things I would have completely forgotten I had even heard about.

The recaps somberly mention silly memes my kids were laughing about, and make major bullet points out of offhand remarks from brief conversations. If a conversation sticks to a single topic, I’ll often get a reasonably good summary of it, with specific facts and numbers highlighted; but just as often, Siri will get confused and mix up several topics or completely mishear a name or phrase.

Apple has four features that it considers part of “audio intelligence":.

Recent findings suggest that music recognition, better known as Shazam. We’ve had a version of this on the Apple Watch for a long time now, although it has some improvements and now identifies music automatically.

Recent findings suggest that sound recognition, which can notify you about doorbells and babies crying. A version of this launched in 2020 as an accessibility feature.

Live Rewind, which gives you an on-wrist transcript of the last 15 seconds of detected speech.

Siri Recaps, which summarizes entire conversations for you to read on your phone.

Recent findings suggest that live Rewind had the flashiest demo from the Apple event: A server rattled off the day’s specials at a restaurant, and then the Apple Watch-wearing diner checked his watch to see a readout of exactly which dishes had just been mentioned. The utility is both obvious and kind of unnecessary: Why wouldn’t you just ask the server to repeat the list while they’re standing right there?

Industry observers note that I haven’t found myself using Live Rewind, except out of curiosity about how the feature works. I discovered that it doesn’t pick up song lyrics very well, and also that by the time I think to check what was just stated in a conversation, more than 15 seconds has passed since the part I was unsure about. I haven’t yet found a reason to use it for real.

But Siri Recaps? Those are both useful and unsettling. I enabled the feature, and decided to test it out later. But since it was on, it dutifully listened in as I picked up my son from school and gave him an update on an ailing family member’s health. We stopped by the library, and along the way we chatted about a variety of things: holiday travel aims, library policies, and the possibility of humans living in space in the future. Siri was listening to it all.

After you're updated to 27.3, go into the Watch app, tap Siri, and turn on Siri Recap. You can set a schedule for when it should listen (for example, 9 a.m. to 5 p.m., if you want it on for the work day but off for the evening). You'll need to set a passcode on your watch, and you'll be guided through a step to upgrade your audio connection. The control center on the watch will have a button you can use to turn Siri recaps on and off at will. To read your recaps, go to the Siri app on your phone.

According to recent reports, as promised, the recaps do not identify speakers. They do not contain an exact transcript, and there is no way to listen to a recording to check what exactly was said. This is probably good for privacy and for relationships; there’s no way to prove that your spouse said such-and-such exact thing. I can also tell people I am not recording them, and technically be correct.

But still: I feel weird publishing the contents of these recaps, because they do contain things that people mentioned to me in what they assumed was a private setting. I had the feature on when I attended a choir practice, and Siri recapped the brief chats I had with other choir members before and after practice. (Interestingly, it did not recap any of the quiet conversations I had with fellow sopranos while the tenors were rehearsing their part. I’m not sure if the watch was unable to hear us over the music, or if Siri is programmed not to listen when music is being played.).

Because speakers aren’t identified, it seems Siri doesn’t know what to do when there is a disagreement. A human note-taker would jot down that Person A made a point in favor of something, and person B made a point against. But when my son and I disagreed about how likely space colonization might be in the future, the recap didn’t reflect the separate positions that were put forth. It summarized the conversation as including “debating the feasibility and timeline of human space colonization and asteroid mining,” which isn’t exactly accurate, but close enough.

When it comes to the content of the discussion, the recap notes a bullet point of “skepticism regarding permanent space colonies within the next 100 years.” It didn’t include my reasons for being skeptical, and didn’t mention my son’s opposing viewpoint at all. If I were using this recap to jog my memory of the conversation, it wouldn’t be all that helpful.

Details are sometimes egregiously incorrect. After a discussion about a family member’s health, the recap had notes on the prognosis of “father.” The family member we discussed is not anybody’s father. Names in general seem to be a problem; I recommended a book to my son, and the recap includes notes about the content of the book, but not its title. The book’s author appears in the introduction to the recap (sort of a summary of a summary), but not in the content of the recap itself where the book is mentioned.

I should probably turn Siri recaps off. It seems wrong to let people chat with me without letting them know that their conversation is being ... well, not technically recorded, but basically recorded.

Sources indicate that but it’s so tempting to leave it on so that I can review my day. Some of the details in the recaps are useful, like the dates that were discussed as options for a holiday party. The recaps will be deleted in about a week (unless I save them to the notes app), so if I want to remind myself of a conversation a few days ago, I should be able to scroll back through my recaps and find it.

Recent findings suggest that I would be a fool to rely on the recaps, though. The most crucial points of a conversation are often left out; Siri doesn’t know what’s actually important, and there’s no way to guide it as to what to pay attention to. Specific details can be wrong, as I mentioned. There’s also no way to control when a “conversation” starts or stops, unless you are turning the recap feature on and off from the watch.

Industry observers note that and there’s more: Not only are names usually omitted (wait, who did she say I should ask about that project?), the few identifiers that make it into the recap, like names of events, are often wrong. Subjects of discussion are often conflated in really unhelpful ways: My husband mentioned paying for certain course registrations for one of our children, and later I talked to that child about an unrelated exam. The recap got all of these things mixed up with each other and was wrong about pretty much every detail. About all the recap could usefully do is to remind me that something about AP U.S. History was discussed. Reading the recaps can be like reliving your day entirely in the passive voice.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that there's been a lot of talk around how long GTA fans have been waiting for the latest entry to launch, but Persona isn't actually that far behind. Persona 5 – in its original state – released over a decade ago on 15th September 2016, and although Persona 6 has now been officially announced, we're none the wiser as to when it will actually come out.

It's likely to finally land at some point in 2027 after the dust has settled from Persona 4 Revival, but according to a recent interview with general producer Kazuhisa Wada (thanks, Nintendo Everything), fans won't have to wait quite so long for the inevitable Persona 7.

It has been revealed that "We will continue to cherish what makes Persona unique, while also embracing changes in the times and needs, and taking on fresh challenges. We aim to be a brand that can grow for 5, 10 years, and beyond.

"Among those projects, the one we’re right now working on is Persona 6. While there’s still limited information I can share, we want to prove the results of all the challenges we’ve faced so far through the game itself. With that in mind, we’re creating something even better than before, and we’re feeling a real sense of accomplishment as we work on it.

Industry observers note that "And Persona 6 is not the end. We are working on various things to ensure that you don’t have to wait as long for the next installment as we have in the past. And in order to make Persona an even bigger IP, we are constantly thinking about creative ideas and developments that will not disappoint your expectations. Please look forward to what’s to come from Persona.”.

Sources indicate that we will look forward to it, Wada-san, thank you sir. Let's keep the focus on Persona 4 Revival and Persona 6 for now though, hm?

In a recent development, it's not a surprising statement, mind you. Game development is taking longer than ever these days, which also makes it more expensive than ever. So a lot of publishers are looking into potential solutions to cut down on dev time and increase the cadence of releases. As long as it doesn't involve handing everything off to AI, we're fine with that.

In a recent development, persona 4 Revival is at the moment scheduled to launch on Switch 2 on 20th May 2027, a few months after other platforms. As for Persona 6, an imminent reveal has been rumoured recently thanks to a backend patch on the official website. Hardly concrete, but it's a start.

According to recent reports, what are your thoughts on Wada-san's comments here? Are you keen for the wait between mainline entries to be slightly shorter in the future? Let us know with a comment.

[source segasammy.co.jp, via nintendoeverything.com].

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ahead of the launch of GTA 6, there was a whole lot of talk online about the Xbox "New Zealand trick" and how people could get early access to the game by switching their regions to New Zealand on Xbox Series X and Xbox Series S.

We mentioned in various articles how it was a risky practice (against Xbox's ToCs), but one that had never traditionally resulted in any widespread bans, and it doesn't seem like either Xbox or Rockstar took any action at first glance.

As it turns out, a lot of people decided to give it a go for the fresh Grand Theft Auto.

This is according to the folks at Ampere Analysis (via The Game Business), who report that over 2.1 million people played GTA 6 in the US and the UK before it was officially released.

In a recent development, as you can see from the graph above, it seems the vast majority of those were based in the United States, followed by the UK, Canada, Brazil and Mexico. Only around 100,000 people tried the trick on PS5 in the U.S. (where it's harder to implement and requires a separate account), whereas 1.5 million of them ended up using it on Xbox.

Ultimately, the existence of the New Zealand trick probably led to a bunch of increased sales for Xbox Series X and Xbox Series S, but it also poses the question of whether Xbox might be forced to put a stop to it on Project Helix and beyond. As much it's a beloved feature, it's also being used in a way that wasn't originally intended.

Let's see what happens in the future, but for now, it's clearly made a lot of people happy this week!

Did you use the New Zealand trick for GTA 6? Let us know your experiences with it in the comments.

My murderous wine merchant whines for a chance at republican rule in Crusader Kings 3’s Silk and Silver expansion, which isn't only about the money

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (2093 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, the tentacles of my trade empire snake up towards France in the west, down towards Africa in the south, and off into Hungary in the east.
  • I’ve shed blood in its name, the blood of someone else named Marco no less.
  • It should, in theory, help that he’s my best mate, thanks to a well-timed feast.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, the tentacles of my trade empire snake up towards France in the west, down towards Africa in the south, and off into Hungary in the east. Yet, I still can’t reach out and grasp the throne that sits right in front of me. I’m Marco Sanudo, and the throne of the serene republic of Venice eludes me.

I’ve shed blood in its name, the blood of someone else named Marco no less. I’ve managed to avoid punishment for that crime, despite the fact it earned me a fiefdom to rule while I’ve tried to up my patrician score enough to be the lucky party the next time a ruling Doge dies in office (or runs out their 10 year term). Sadly, Doge Leonardo, the mysterious masked lord who’s had an iron grip on power since the first couple of old blokes to hold the position in this playthrough popped their clogs, is proving incredibly tough to oust.

It should, in theory, help that he’s my best mate, thanks to a well-timed feast. It certainly did in being granted a pardon for offing that other Marco, but not even that and a plague which infected nearly everyone in the realm aside from me have paved the way to Dogedom. In the meantime, I’ve striven to gain wealth and influence. I’ve worked up to having four trade routes running at once, with goods like wine, iron, and textiles flowing from market to market across southern Europe and bringing a steady supply of coin back to my Venetian estate. I’ve built trade posts at the extremities of my routes, giving me the option of starting from further afield and reaching new lands if the cash flow dries up closer to home.

It has been revealed that this is where Crusader Kings 3’s Silk and Silver expansion has blended a bit with the game’s traditional feudal moneymaking to supercharge my coffers. The land holding I killed a dude for, the Proveditorate of Zara, means I’ve also had tax money from modern day Croatia to add to both my trade profits and the income my domicile generates on its own. I am, as the medieval kids say, minted.

Industry observers note that getting to the point of serious pocket clinkage is, as you might imagine given Silk and Silver’s focus on filling the game’s world with travelling merchant companies and wheeler-dealing republican patrician families, the beating heart of the expansion. A near-constant stream of notifications about prices of different goods I’m trying to hawk in different locations encourage me to regularly prune and re-work my routes so that max profits are being earned and no carrying capacity’s being wasted. The bubbling up of wars and plagues impacts prices in affected cities, making it a never-ending battle if you’re desperate to optimise everything within an inch of its life. I’ve found that degree of micromanagement unnecessary if the goal is just to keep a decent profit margin ticking over. Just remember to replace the trader assigned to a route if they die, recall them every few years so they don’t stress themselves to death, and check in every so often to re-evaluate whether you’re running goods that are suitably in demand.

In a recent development, if you stick at it for a decent amount of time, with a certain type of good - alcohol or jewellery, for example - your expertise in dealing in them increases, making it easier to sell for better prices. Trade routes left running between the same markets also gain boons from being in place for a long time, offering a counterpoint to rejigging them every five seconds to wring out a few more coins. Most of my routes have run along a path that includes stops at four markets, with the occasional location boasting a monopoly I’ve bargained for with the local ruler, so I don’t have to worry about competition at every stop.

Sources indicate that when you’re playing as a merchant who isn’t locked into the ruling inner circle of a republic, making your routes as lengthy as possible is one of the three moneymaking areas your firm can specialise in. That first one’s caravaneering, and is the one I leant into in a non-Marco Sanudo playthrough. Beyond that, you can become an expert loan shark, lending cash to rulers or paying their ransoms in order to recoup interest and collect hooks you can use for favours. Manufacturing expensive artifacts that can be sold individually to collectors for a profit is the third option. The latter two I’ve only dabbled in a little bit as of writing, having earned enough gold mostly from caravanneering to buy the land containing the city with my home market and be anointed a Sheikh. So, beginning as a landless merchant is a nice alternative to Crusader Kings 3’s long-established wandering adventurer starting point, with both allowing you to work your way up from lowly serf to landed lordly dynasty in your location of choice.

Industry observers note that if you’re after a more specific historical scenario, Silk and Silver has Guelphs and Ghibellines. This is where we find Marco Sanudo, as well as the other patrician family head I’ve played as thus far, Speronella Dalesmanni. The setup is that the Pope and the Holy Roman Emperor have had a bit of a tiff, essentially rooted in who should have certain powers, with different cities and powerful families in northern Italy taking either the Guelph (Pope-likers) or Ghibelline (Holy Roman Empire-enjoyers) side depending on what suits their goals or principles. I’ll be honest, aside from being another way to easily earn friends or enemies in the ruthless crucible of merchant republican politics, where votes and reputation-bolstering aid from other nobles are key, the situation’s not had a hugely obvious bearing on my playthroughs thus far.

I think the closest it’s come is during my Dalesmanni run, if largely due to the existence of the By God Alone expansion allowing a upcoming branch of Catholicism, dubbed Italian Christianity, to be created. The initial conversion push from the bishop responsible led a number of my fellow northern Italian nobles away from the Roman Rite headed by his Popeliness, making the Guelph/Ghibelline split more clearly defined.

According to recent reports, in the early hours of both my Sanudo and Dalesmanni playthroughs, I’ve been far more focused on simply trying to push the respective patrician families up the hill from posh toffs with naught but a vote and a manor to elected rulers of their great cities, with land holdings to match. Speronella’s situation in Padua is made incredibly tough by the fact she’s a woman in a world where every succession rule is designed to put blokes first, so I’ve had more success with Marco and his quest to become the Doge of Venice.

Recent findings suggest that as the head of a patrician family, one of select few elite clans who steer the oligarchical republic, I was faced with earning Marco enough respect among his fellow family heads that they’d consider voting him to the top of the succession list, thus securing his power whenever the current Doge got the boot. Pulling that off, while also not kowtowing to the requests and schemes of those same peers, isn’t easy. A large cocktail of factors go into determining whether another noble likes you enough to vote in support of your succession. There’s your patrician rating, which is upped by doing things which specifically show you to be good at this Italian noble house lark, such as establishing trade monopolies for the republic, gaining the Pope’s favour, or having close relatives who also hold key positions in the republic. However, how close a friendship you have with the target and how their character traits align with you also play a huge rule.

Industry observers note that thus it was that, at one point, Marco was best mates with the current Doge and had a decent patrician rating, but had only amassed 68 of the 72 points needed for said Doge to vote for him because the Doge was generous, and therefore didn’t care for Marco’s ambitiousness. That same Doge either liked or respected Marco enough to grant him a council position and the status of regent, but he would not back Marco to replace him permanently for love nor money. This is the same man who liked Marco so much that when I pulled off that not-so-sneaky murder on another noble house head in order to inherit the keys to the Proveditorate of Zara, the Doge was instantly willing to pardon me and prevent Marco suffering any punishment for the crime.

Sources indicate that not even a couple of serious plagues hitting Venice, which at one point had all three people ahead of Marco in the queue suffering from smallpox, could get him on that throne. Eventually, it took a bit of lucky timing when his Doge mate died of old age - a few years after beating smallpox - to finally install Marco as Doge. Given that delayed promotion, as of writing I’ve not yet had enough time in the significant chair to give a proper verdict on how it differs from regular feudal rulerdom in the long run.

What I can do instead is tell you a bit about the fun of council votes. The same pool of voters who in a republic like Venice, get a say in who succeeds the ruler, also vote on the passage of laws and decrees. One proposal you can put forward is a vote to change who exactly is allowed a seat in this voting pool. It defaults to just being heads of patrician families, but can be extended to include all vassals, or tightened up so only the Doge’s councillors or the ruler themselves have a say, that being the way despotism lies. As you can imagine, passing a change to who can vote can drastically change the state of play, either tightening up the number of folks who might oppose or support you, or bringing latest folks into play in a fashion that dilutes individual power, but gives you more pieces on the board to mind or manipulate to your advantage.

Recent findings suggest that I’ve found it suitably tough to orchestrate successful votes to change laws and customs which medieval Italian noble families, expectedly, have firmly entrenched stances on. Getting rid of checks and balances, such as the requirement to vote on banishments or wars - so the Doge can rule as a despot - has proven one such challenge, as has changing laws governing men being prioritised over women. I tried to pass equal succession as a substitute for men being put first while playing as Speronella, but met an insurmountable wall of resistance due to the region’s culture and faith. So, all I could do was try to put my young male heir in the best position possible to make the sorts of gains I couldn’t.

Much easier to weasel into place, either through some canny swaying or the offering of hooks, are laws giving state backing or other priority to trading in certain types of goods. Alcohol, for instance, which certainly hasn’t hurt the profits of Marco’s two wine trade routes.

According to recent reports, thus, cash continues to flow through the tentacles of my trade empire in sizable globs. As he’s now Doge, I’ve got Marco using the ample funds of Venice’s treasury to build a latest piazza and have him focused on making the city’s already-strong trade league even more formidable, by attracting new members from the few other northern Italian blocs.

While I’m fairly sure there are folks who’ll find Silk and Silver's constant barrage of trade route notifications annoying, or that their power-grabbing skills and sheer multitude of money-making means combine to make playthroughs less challenging than they could be, so far I've found it another enjoyably sonorous string to Crusader Kings 3’s bow. Above all else, playing as a merchant gives more reason to invest in stewardship skills beyond just maximising your tax yields, while the republican politics of the DLC's main region fleshes out rewarding intrigue-focused builds. Diplomacy and martial skills are less key, but still have their place at times.

If you’re an absolute stickler for historical accuracy, you may well find other things to gripe about, but aside from the Guelph and Ghibelline conflict fading into the background, I’ve found plenty to like in my quest to become top Doge.

The next Xbox, Project Helix, is a console and "not a PC" says Microsoft, as it clarifies that computational power isn't sole focus this time

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (863 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Eurogamer
