📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Microsoft has stressed that its next-generation Xbox console, Project Helix, "is not a PC that can also play console games", but rather "a console that is also capable of playing games from your PC".
  • Recent findings suggest that the details come from a Microsoft-produced Xbox magazine made available digitally yesterday, and a Helix-related feature speaking to Xbox vice president of next generation, Jason Ronald.
  • "We're very clear on the design goal," Ronald later added.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Microsoft has stressed that its next-generation Xbox console, Project Helix, "is not a PC that can also play console games", but rather "a console that is also capable of playing games from your PC". The tech giant has also underlined the importance of using gen-AI-adjacent "neural rendering" technology going forwards, and a desire to remove "all the barriers of play that have historically existed" - notably in making the past generations of games playable.

Recent findings suggest that the details come from a Microsoft-produced Xbox magazine made available digitally yesterday, and a Helix-related feature speaking to Xbox vice president of next generation, Jason Ronald. "When we think about Project Helix, it's really designed to be the ultimate gaming machine," Ronald stated, "one that removes all the barriers of play that have historically existed. My entire library is accessible to me. I'm able to bring four generations of my Xbox library and progression with me and have it available instantly. And we remove the arbitrary constraints between console and PC games.

"We're very clear on the design goal," Ronald later added. "Helix is designed to be a console that is also capable of playing games from your PC. It is not a PC that can also play console games. The goal is making it easy, intuitive, and instant to access my games. But if you're a hardcore gamer or a power user who wants to have that deeper level of customisability across settings and performance options, you can absolutely go do it.".

Notably, Ronald seemed to suggest that Helix - the console, not the handheld; "Helix" refers to a couple of machines - isn't solely focused on computational grunt. Indeed, he said the next generation wasn't about hitting 8K resolutions and 240 hertz frame-rates, but instead leaning on technologies like "neural rendering" - i.e. generative-AI - and encouraging innovation.

It has been revealed that "It's about deeper immersion," Ronald said. "It is about leveraging latest technical advancements such as neural rendering to deliver a new level of visual fidelity in more efficient and innovative ways. It's about new kinds of games and new game experiences that we haven't been able to do before. What excites me about the future is the idea of entirely new types of games that have never been possible before, delivered through all the innovation in the silicon and the hardware and the platform that we're delivering.".

According to recent reports, while referencing the global component shortage and exorbitant prices of computer hardware, he added: "This is a major reason why we're really focused on advancements like neural rendering because it's an entirely latest way to generate a frame without requiring more computational horsepower, additional memory, and things like that. I think you're going to see more innovation over the next three to five years than you've seen in the last 10 years.".

Xbox boss Asha Sharma also recently talked up the importance of generative-AI-sounding technology in Xbox's future, saying "too many ideas never become games", and that "a single person will soon be able to wield capabilities that once required entire nations".

Another key part of Xbox's Helix vision is compatibility and game preservation. "Game preservation is core to Xbox," Ronald went as far as to say. "Not only do we feel like it's the right thing for the industry, we feel a deep responsibility as one of its biggest platforms and publishers. For the first 30 years of game development, nobody really thought about game preservation when they were designing their hardware, when they were building their games." Xbox is apparently working with game-makers to ensure games can not only be played now but also 20 to 30 years into the future.

The other key facet of Microsoft's push the familiar Play Anywhere mantra, whereby one game can be played across multiple devices, maintaining your game-progress as you go. This is fundamental to Microsoft's handheld-and-console Helix proposal, and something we've seen the tech giant dry-run with the Xbox ROG Ally X handheld. "It's this notion that not only does my library move with me, but my progress moves with me as well," Ronald mentioned. "Because I fully expect that when I'm in the middle of an 80-hour RPG, if I'm 25 hours into that and I want to play it on another device, I should be able to instantly resume from where I was. Those are things that today are becoming more common, but I think in the future it's going to be a baseline expectation of all players.".

Recent findings suggest that ronald wouldn't be drawn on the issue of price regarding Project Helix - a recent report suggested Helix could be priced up to $1800 - referring to it only as both "a challenging time" but an "exciting one", because "we have to invent entirely latest technology to continue to advance the state-of-the-art while also continuing to make things accessible and affordable". Ronald also wouldn't reference a release date, though the report referenced above suggested the handheld Helix machine will release next holiday, 2027, and the console Helix machine the year after. The next generation, then, seems to be around the corner.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that the wait for GTA 6 is finally over.
  • Josh's credentials are in little doubt.
  • When you're reviewing any video game, time is the biggest enemy.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that the wait for GTA 6 is finally over. Except for a lucky few, the wait actually ended several weeks ago. Early access for the purpose of reviewing GTA 6 kicked off in plenty of time to allow select press and creators to experience the game in full ahead of launch. One such early adopter was GamesRadar+'s Editor-in-Chief, Josh West, the writer responsible for our five-star GTA 6 review. For this member-exclusive article, I asked him to offer a peek behind the curtain about what it was like to cast a verdict on the biggest entertainment event of the decade.

Josh's credentials are in little doubt. He states he's played every single GTA game - "yes, even the ones on PS1" - and that he attended the midnight launch of GTA 4. He also reviewed GTA 5 back in 2013, but says that was a uniquely stressful experience. While it was relatively easy to keep GTA 6 under wraps, during his venture to Los Santos, he says "I lived in a small shared house with five other people. Keeping the fact that I had a copy of the game weeks in advance a secret, in an environment where nobody knocked before entering a room, still stresses me out thinking about it today.".

When you're reviewing any video game, time is the biggest enemy.

"Around 120 hours" of playtime was logged by GTA 6's in-game counter when Josh sat down to write his review, though he claims the PS5's internal clock had recorded "far longer" than that. A few-weeks-long runway might seem like plenty of time to check out even a game of that significant size, but once you've factored in the need to sleep, eat, and fulfil other "demands of life," Josh says finishing the review ahead of deadline remained "a bit of a highwire act.".

"Time is the biggest enemy," he notes. The deadline around a major review is pretty firm, dictated by an embargo that no-one can publish ahead of, but which no-one wants to be stuck behind. That "does sometimes mean you aren't able to engage with a world in the way you would if you were playing in an everyday environment." With the clock ticking in real life, whiling away the hours just hanging out with Jason and Lucia is something you might not want to commit too much time to.

That's particularly ironic in a game like this, where a non-trivial slice of gameplay does revolve around "sitting there with Lucia on the couch, watching TV shows and playing in-universe video games." And as a double-whammy, investing in your downtime is a genuinely useful activity: Focus, Josh indicates, is the game's most useful skill, but it's also the hardest to upgrade, and doing so usually requires completing tasks that require some mental effort - playing minigolf, hitting the shooting range, meditating, fishing. These all take up valuable review time, but they're also a pivotal part of the game experience that can't be skipped over if you want a full impression.

Despite being pushed towards the end by the hands of Father Time, Josh claims there's plenty left to see: "Even with the story complete and 80% overall game completion, there's still so much of GTA 6 that I'm yet to see, discover, and master." Even once the review was filed and the game was out, he was "exploring some corner of the map that you'd honestly have no reason to go anywhere near," where "I got dragged into a weird and utterly wild scripted encounter that is among my favourites in GTA 6.".

As much as there's still stuff to discover in the wilds of Leonida after more than 120 hours, Josh notes he knew he was in for something special "just a few hours in." When I asked what the first sign that GTA 6 truly had 'the sauce' was, he pointed to an innocuous encounter in the Keys: "I spent what little cash I had to make modifications to JAson's old Vapid '70 Ganado - new paint, new engine, the works. Within minutes of pulling out of the mod shop some random driver made an illegal turn and hit me. I pulled the car over to the side of the road, got out and started checking for damage, and got annoyed that the money was for nothing. It was at that point I realised I had been fully captured by this virtual reality, and that feeling never really went away.".

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that I am nothing if not entirely predictable.
  • It has been revealed that GTA 5, once it made its way to PC, was always a game I played both with a keyboard and mouse and with a controller plugged in.
  • It was the same with Red Dead Redemption 2, a game I completely avoided until it finally came to the PC.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that I am nothing if not entirely predictable. I've waited 13 years to play a newly introduced Grand Theft Auto game and the first thing I do when I finally get around to booting GTA 6—and definitely not spoofing my home address to access it early—is jam a mouse and keyboard into my Xbox Series X just to see.

It has been revealed that GTA 5, once it made its way to PC, was always a game I played both with a keyboard and mouse and with a controller plugged in. Keeb and rodent for shooting, especially in the first-person mode, and the controller for just getting about in the game world. It was a real best of both worlds kinda thing that the PC does so well.

It was the same with Red Dead Redemption 2, a game I completely avoided until it finally came to the PC. Keyboard and mouse for runnin' and gunnin' and a controller for horsin' around. Yeehaw.

Industry observers note that so, I was hoping—hoping against hope, really—that I could just do the same with GTA 6. I was hoping that I could just plug in my little Mountain keyboard and my DeathAdder mouse, and it would just work.

Recent findings suggest that sadly no, there is no mouse and keyboard support for GTA 6. There is for Xbox, and my keyboard works fine just in the home screens, but as soon as you hit the game itself… nada. Keyboard and mouse support is still very much an occasional thing for Microsoft's console. It is supported, but it's on a per-game basis where devs have to actively code support into their Xbox versions of a title in order for a keyboard and mouse to work.

Sources indicate that it's not actually that rare—some 450 games, and significant games such as Cyberpunk 2077 and Alan Wake 2, have some level of support for one or both peripherals. But it is certainly not something Rockstar has spent any time putting in place when it was spending an extra year optimising the game after the delayed release. Which is a shame, given that the company has gone to great lengths to add a huge level of detail to its world to the point it almost feels like it's thought of everything.

In a recent development, more frustrating given that right now I bet there are Rockstar developers playing the game on keyboard and mouse in internal PC-only builds of the game. Would I have sacrificed sitting on my comfy sofa playing it writ large on my living room wall through my 4K projector just to sit at my desk with a keyboard and mouse? Maybe. It would have certainly felt like I was playing it on PC.

The PC Gamer Circuit Breaker newsletter breaks down the latest PC gaming tech, and finds you the best deals on the best products.

Something else Rockstar hasn't put into the game is any steering wheel control. Jacob, as a racing fan, tried to get his PlayStation wheelbase running on his PS5 copy of the game… but alas that is unsupported, too. Which was a source of frustration for him as he co-opted his partner in carrying his sim rig into his living room to try it out and now she is refusing to help put it back after his failure.

Sources indicate that but this is a situation that might have to change moving forward. The next-gen Xbox machine, codenamed Helix has already been confirmed as being able to play PC games. In a recent interview with Jason Ronald, Xbox VP of Next Gen, this was again reiterated.

"We're very clear on the design goal: Helix is designed to be a console that is also capable of playing games from your PC," states Ronald. "It is not a PC that can also play console games.".

In a recent development, this means it's going to have to support PC games, and that potentially means baked in support for keyboard and mouse in the hardware itself, rather than enabled on a per-title basis. After all, PC games kinda take those inputs for granted, no? So, maybe Red Dead Redemption 3 on Project Helix might come with keyboard and mouse support from the get-go, even if it's not necessarily released on PC straight away.

Still, for GTA 6 right now, basically it's controller or nothing, so make sure to get yourself a good pad—that's one of the biggest upgrades I've made to my setup for GTA 6.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

After years of dominating Netflix's top 10 list, Squid Game finally came to an end last year with its third and final season. But the story may not be over after all, as series creator Hwang Dong-hyuk notes he might one day return to the franchise.

According to recent reports, "As far as I’m concerned, someday I’ll get back to Squid Game," remarked Hwang at the Doha Film Festival (Variety). "When I have a great idea, I’ll make another one." However, Hwang pointed out that he doesn't actually own Squid Game. "Unfortunately, it’s not mine… Netflix owns the IP, so it’s not my decision how to expand.".

Sources indicate that following a desperate man named Seong Gi-hun, who, alongside 455 other players strapped for cash, enters a deadly game to win a hefty prize, the dystopian series promptly became a hit over at Netflix. The first season debuted to a near-perfect Rotten Tomatoes score, and the show is still Netflix's most-watched series ever, per Tudum.

It has been revealed that the idea for the series came to Hwang when he faced financial troubles of his own. "When I first wrote the script, the beginning point of my creative process was when I was poor," he remarked. "I didn’t have much money and imagined: What if it was me? Would I enter this kind of competition and try to win the prize? I was so broke in 2009. I was so broke. I only had like $5 in my account.".

However, after the huge success of the first season, Hwang remarked he felt the pressure to make a second and third season just as good. "There was pressure from Netflix," added Hwang, "We were always getting questions: 'Where is Season 2? Season 3?' It was a nightmare.” However, Hwang said he never tries to "make something that people like," adding, "I always try to make what I like to make while at the same time hoping and praying people like what I like to make. If I lose that mindset, I’ll go crazy.".

Netflix already released the American reality show Squid Game: The Challenge based on the series. Soon after Squid Game season 3, the streamer also announced a US remake from Gone Girl director David Fincher, which was hinted at in the Squid Game season 3 ending featuring Cate Blanchett as the newly introduced recruiter. However, reports suggest that the show may now be dead.

It has been revealed that you can stream Squid Game in full on Netflix now. For more, see where it places on our list of the best Netflix shows, and keep up with new TV shows on the way.

  • Let's review what we already know: there is a conservative estimate of 10 million pre-orders for Rockstar's latest game floating around - something buoyed by comments from Take-Two boss Strauss Zelnick - and, even by the company's lofty expectations, we know the game is tracking "well above expectations" when it comes to pre-orders.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

We all know the story of GTA 5 making more than $1 billion in the first three days it was on sale, right? At the time, Take-Two believed this to be the fastest any entertainment property had achieved the impressive milestone - music and films included. It made history, and with ease. And it looks like GTA 6 is going to do even better.

Recent findings suggest that at least, that's according to one analyst, Joost van Dreunen, a senior data analyst and great writer/numbers diviner who wrote some predictions in his respected SuperJoost PlayList newsletter. "My prediction: Take-Two reveals opening-weekend sales above $2 billion by Monday, 23rd November," he wrote. And you know what? I reckon he's onto something.

Let's review what we already know: there is a conservative estimate of 10 million pre-orders for Rockstar's latest game floating around - something buoyed by comments from Take-Two boss Strauss Zelnick - and, even by the company's lofty expectations, we know the game is tracking "well above expectations" when it comes to pre-orders.

We also know a lot of people are shelling out for the slightly more pricey Ultimate Edition (£90). So many people are opting for the more expensive version, in fact, that Take-Two revised its financial forecast up to $3.5bn for the next financial quarter, thanks to "recurrent consumer spending" (something Zelnick clarified in an investor's call is explicitly linked to the Ultimate Edition). 10 million pre-orders, at roughly $100 per copy - that's $1 billion right off the bat.

"That’s two days faster than its predecessor," van Dreunen noted, "and largely before anyone has even played the game." That other $1bn will come over the weekend. And then, per the analyst, the game will sell roughly another 28 million copies over the course of the first year it's on sale. "My forecast puts first-year sales at 38 million copies, only modestly ahead of GTA 5’s 35 million. The real difference may be how much revenue each player generates over the years that follow.".

But it's what follows in the newsletter that intrigues me most. "At the high end, [GTA 6] may just lift the entire industry with it," wrote van Dreunen. "In the face of AI slop and shitty mobile games that exist only to extract revenue, it will offer a reprieve. At a time when the industry is increasingly focused on making games cheaper and monetising players more aggressively, Rockstar is about to demonstrate the enduring appeal of spending a fortune to make something people actually want to play.".

So, even if you're dubious about the game and Rockstar's motivations for selling as many copies as possible, the launch of GTA 6 could be something that gives the industry a much-needed jolt of life, in the face of rampant layoffs and shrinking talent pools.

Sources indicate that it's not all sunshine and rainbows ahead for Rockstar, though: amongst the frenzy of launch activity, Rockstar has been embroiled in legal action after it was accused of union busting following the firing of over 30 employees. The case's conclusion will be determined this week, as the game goes on sale.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Latest multiplayer game Spirit Crossing offers up a visually blissful, but inwardly draconian world in which other people are not allowed to talk to you – indeed, not permitted access to the visible electromagnetic spectrum – unless you have given them a high five.
  • Recent findings suggest that deign to slap somebody's hand, and they'll pop into colour and be able to join you for various activities.
  • There's nothing forcing you to do any of this in manufacturer, mind.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Latest multiplayer game Spirit Crossing offers up a visually blissful, but inwardly draconian world in which other people are not allowed to talk to you – indeed, not permitted access to the visible electromagnetic spectrum – unless you have given them a high five. By default, players appear to each other as shadows, all exploring a skybound landscape of magic animals and layer-cake mountains that reminds me of both Sable and The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom.

Recent findings suggest that deign to slap somebody's hand, and they'll pop into colour and be able to join you for various activities. For example, going fishing, playing instruments round the campfire, playing dress-up and pulling emotes in group photos, bouncing around on strangely inflated yaks, or questing forth to heal troubled spirits. There's some material gathering and crafting, and there are recurring storms that make the ambience more threatening, but overcoming a challenge doesn't feel like the point of Spirit Crossing. The "missions" are just an excuse to hang out together.

There's nothing forcing you to do any of this in manufacturer, mind. "Stay a mysterious shadow, lend a hand when you feel like it, and disappear before anyone can make it weird," the devs explain, adding a hug emoji to make plain that they don't think you're some kind of smelly misanthrope for shunning other players.

I, personally, am a smelly misanthrope, and will only ever appear in your game as a skulking opacity, peering through the window of your personal gingerbread house, with its tastefully accessorised lava lamps and throw rugs. No, I will not join you for a group hang-glider tour. No, I do not want to play the banjo with you. You will experience me only as the nagging sensation of being watched, while you chat to the local "Stylesmith" about fetching rucksack patterns.

Spirit Crossing has an upfront cost that "gives players full access to the complete game experience in perpetuity", but you can also take out a subscription for some cosmetic items and access to a "limited resource exchange shop". They're avoiding traditional microtransactions, which is nice.

It has been revealed that spry Fox are also the developers of Cozy Grove - "the best grove since Byker", wrote Graham, in one of his regular 'senior moments'. I myself know them as the studio behind wintry puzzler Road Not Taken, with its randomised woodlands, and block-merging city builder Triple Town, with its unexpectedly terrifying bears. Little about Spirit Crossing seems terrifying, unless you count the shadow loitering at the edge of your conversation pit.

Recent findings suggest that you can read more about the game on Steam. I find Spirit Crossing quite novel, especially when it dispenses with the WholeCosy "discover your inner fashonista" stuff and leans into the supernatural elements: I like the idea of hunkering by the campfire during a storm, watching the clouds hurtle past. Still, I'm disappointed to hear that Spry Fox have made use of generative AI during its creation.

As has been pointed out to us on Bluesky, the developers called on Anthropic's Claude tools for various behind-the-scenes tasks - the example they give in a Discord post is editing several config files at once. There's no disclosure on the game's Steam page because Spry Fox haven't used AI tools to generate any of the art or music - Valve rewrote Steam's disclosure requirements in January to exempt the usage of generative AI for "efficiency gains", which the above presumably falls under.

It's hardly a full-throated endorsement of generative AI, but it still forms part of a political and cultural project I consider reckless and morbid. For a longer account of my objections, albeit one that doesn't cover Claude in particular, here's my longform thinkywangle from July last year.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

One first-party title from the GameCube library that's well and truly outlived this particular Nintendo generation is Super Smash Bros. Melee, and today happens to be the game's 25th anniversary in Japan.

Sources indicate that after introducing fans to the series in 1999 on the N64, Masahiro Sakurai and the team at HAL Laboratory & Nintendo rolled out this newly introduced, improved, and faster take on the all-star Nintendo fighter in November 2001. Not only was it a popular couch game, but Melee went on to have an incredibly successful run as a competitive game.

According to Nintendo's official data, Melee is officially the "best-selling game of all time" for the GameCube, shifting over seven million copies worldwide, with the system itself selling 21.74 million units during its lifetime.

This particular entry was so influential within the Smash scene that it led to Nintendo re-releasing the GameCube controller and making newer entries in the series compatible with this same pad, as it was the preferred pick for any serious or pro player.

Industry observers note that to this day, the game's competitive scene is still going strong, with game's meta continuing to evolve, and players like "Hungrybox" (the famous Jigglypuff main) are still knocking about. Of course, there have also been plenty of scandals within the competitive space over the years, but Melee continues to thrive, and is still capable of packing out events across the globe.

Industry observers note that so, on behalf of the team here at Nintendo Life, here's to another 25 years of duking it out. Oh, and if Nintendo hasn't already got something planned, now would be the perfect time to add Melee to the Switch 2's GameCube library. For North America, the game's 25th anniversary takes place in early December.

Feel free to share your memories of Smash Bros. Melee in the comments. Are you still playing it 25 years on? Let us know.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • GTA 6 has been censored to a fairly large extent in Japan, where the country's strict ratings system often sees nudity, sexual content, and graphic violence be toned down or removed entirely in video games.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

GTA 6 has been censored to a fairly large extent in Japan, where the country's strict ratings system often sees nudity, sexual content, and graphic violence be toned down or removed entirely in video games.

To be clear, GTA 6 has been given Japan's highest 18+ age rating — but it's still had to make changes in order to ensure its release in the region.

For starters, Rockstar's latest is packed with full-on nudity — to a degree never before seen in a mainstream release — but in Japan, it's apparently impossible to remove the underwear of main characters Jason and Lucia, even when they're taking a shower.

The same is true of NPCs — everyone's always wearing at least one layer to cover up their privates.

Needless to say, the game's numerous sex scenes have also been censored. Again, it's a case of keeping clothes on — but some specific scenes have actually been cut completely.

It has been revealed that violence is next on the list. GTA 6 obviously features a lot of bloodshed but it's also rather gory, with accurate depictions of dismemberment and lethal physical trauma. It can all come across as particularly gruesome given how realistic the game looks.

It has been revealed that in Japan, it seems as though most of this stuff is scaled back. There's less blood spray in general, and spilled blood doesn't stay in place very long.

It's a little unclear just how far this censorship of violence goes, but it's not uncommon for Japan to remove things like dismemberment — especially if a game's got a grounded setting.

For what it's worth, GTA 6 does have several settings that let you change the amount of blood and gore that's on display. I assume that in Japan, these settings are applied at a censored standard by default.

According to recent reports, interestingly, though, drug use seemingly hasn't been touched. Japan's got very strict anti-drug laws, but illegal goods are still totally usable in GTA 6.

Latest Update: Corsair Sabre V3 Pro PureVector Ergo review

⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that the aim-assisting PureVector technology in this mouse promises a lot, but in my case it fails to deliver, as my aim doesn't improve from turning it on.
  • PC Gamer's got your back Our experienced team dedicates many hours to every review, to really get to the heart of what matters most to you.
  • According to recent reports, corsair is continuing the 2026 trend of brands pushing out fresh and innovative mouse technologies.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that the aim-assisting PureVector technology in this mouse promises a lot, but in my case it fails to deliver, as my aim doesn't improve from turning it on. It's a solid, lightweight, competitive mouse regardless, but it's too expensive for what it is without delivering the PureVector promise.

PC Gamer's got your back Our experienced team dedicates many hours to every review, to really get to the heart of what matters most to you. Find out more about how we evaluate games and hardware.

According to recent reports, corsair is continuing the 2026 trend of brands pushing out fresh and innovative mouse technologies. In this case, it's all in the 'PureVector' part of the name. In partnership with AimLabs, Corsair has made a mouse that can adjust sensitivity in different directions to tailor it to your movements and help you aim better.

According to recent reports, that's the claim, anyway. In practice, I've found that PureVector hasn't improved my aim, both subjectively while gaming and objectively based on multiple AimLabs tests. Some pro players that Corsair highlights claim it's helped them, so your mileage may vary.

Apart from PureVector, though, the mouse itself deserves some attention, as it's still a very performant, lightweight mouse for competitive gaming. It has some upgrades compared to its predecessor, the Sabre V2 Pro, too.

✅ You want to try the latest tech: You might get better results than I did with PureVector. It tailors sensor sensitivity in different directions based on how you aim.

❌ You want good value for the basics: If you just want a comfy mouse with solid build quality that performs well, you can find something of better value elsewhere.

The aim-assisting PureVector technology in this mouse promises a lot, but in my case it fails to deliver, as my aim doesn't improve from turning it on. It's a solid, lightweight, competitive mouse regardless, but it's too expensive for what it is without delivering on the PureVector promise.

Replacement skates, USB-A to USB-C cable, wireless dongle, AimLabs PureVector software integration.

Sources indicate that in most ways, the Sabre V3 Pro PureVector Ergo is your standard competitive gaming mouse: lightweight, few frills, simple design, good sensor. It is lighter than most competitive mice with a solid shell, though a little heavier than its predecessor, the Sabre V2 Pro.

In a recent development, setting aside the PureVector aiming shenanigans for a moment, probably the biggest improvement compared to the Sabre V2 Pro is its battery life, which has been doubled. Apart from that, you're getting a 42,000 DPI sensor, optical clicks, and some bigger replacement skates included in the box.

Industry observers note that now we come to the main attraction: PureVector. Corsair has designed the mouse's internals and firmware to permit different sensitivities in different directions. So, for instance, it can move slightly slower horizontally than vertically.

According to recent reports, corsair has worked with AimLabs to let you test your aiming in the latter software and then have the mouse adjust your directional sensitivity for you. The PureVector software within AimLabs has been made with the help of a bunch of aiming data (over 4 billion data points, apparently) and machine learning. The end result is, in theory, a mouse that can tailor its sensitivity in different directions to stop you over-shooting or under-shooting your target.

The PC Gamer Circuit Breaker newsletter breaks down the latest PC gaming tech, and finds you the best deals on the best products.

Again, in theory, this should also save you time when you aim, and Corsair claims it can save more time than reducing the latency of clicks—the latter is, for example, what we see the Logitech G Pro X2 Superstrike and X3 Superstrike focusing on.

It's worth noting that Corsair highlights a number of pro players who say they've benefitted from this upcoming tech. However, for my part, I haven't noticed a difference.

According to recent reports, for reference, I play Counter-Strike 2 at about FaceIt Level 7 or Premier 18–20,000 rating (approx. top 15%). I'm far from a pro, but I'm far from the worst. In-game, I didn't notice any difference between my aim with PureVector set up and with it disabled.

I also repeatedly tested my aim in the AimLabs SpiderShot Precision test, and I actually had slightly better results using another mouse without PureVector (the SteelSeries Sensei Pro), and the latter mouse my hand was less familiar with.

More than this, though, I can't help but feel that it's a bit of a band-aid solution to poor aim. If you're overshooting your shots when you aim left, for instance, you could get PureVector to lower your sensitivity in that direction. But why not instead work on training your hand not to overshoot? That way, having good aim won't be dependent on using this one mouse, and you can get used to aiming consistently in different directions.

Sources indicate that pureVector aside, the Sabre V3 Pro performs well. The sensor is great and feels very responsive. Ditto the newly introduced optical mouse clicks. I have no complaints about its performance as a general mouse, I just don't see the use in PureVector myself. Of course, your mileage may vary, as it seems to have for some pro players.

One area where the Sabre V3 Pro does particularly shine, just like the Sabre V2 Pro, is in its light weight. This latest iteration feels even sturdier than the previous one and still manages to be lighter than most competitive gaming mice.

Sources indicate that battery life is a definite selling point of the Sabre V3 Pro PureVector. It's a lot better than I was expecting. The Sabre V2 Pro can only manage about 70 hours at 1 kHz, and this upcoming one doubles that to 140 hours.

In a recent development, I think Corsair has struck a great balance here, because it's not as light as the V2—which was 36 g—but 41 g is still incredibly light, and I'd much rather have the bigger battery than shave off those few extra grams. You're not getting any fancy wireless charging or hot-swappable batteries here, but 140 hours of battery life is great.

The Corsair Sabre V3 Pro PureVector Ergo is, as its excruciatingly long name suggests, pretty ergonomic. It's not the biggest ergo mouse I've used—the Zowie EC2-DW and SteelSeries Rival Pro both feel a bit bigger in-hand—but it still feels comfy under my medium-sized palm.

There's also a non-ergo, symmetrical version for the same price, and you can get carbon fiber or magnesium versions for each, if you're willing to spend even more ($200 and $230, respectively).

I like the lightweight ergonomic version, though. Its slightly smaller size, combined with its light weight, also means holding it in a fingertip or claw grip doesn't feel too bad, which isn't something you can say about many ergonomic mice. Palm grip is still the main intention here, though. Playing Counter-Strike on low sensitivity feels great.

Build quality is decent, too, which is a bit of a relief because the previous version, the Sabre V2 Pro, sacrificed some on this front to achieve its 'ultralight' status. There's no creak or flex along the sides, and only a slight bit of flex on the underside. The side buttons feel great, with no pre-travel, and the scroll wheel has well-defined steps.

There is some pre-travel to the left- and right-mouse buttons, however, and they don't feel as satisfying to press as some other mice like the Razer Viper V4 Pro or SteelSeries Rival Pro. They're far from bad, just not quite up to the standard of some other expensive gaming mice I've tried.

According to recent reports, the version I've got here, the 'Ergo' one, is pretty plain and looks quite similar to its predecessor, the Sabre V2 Pro. It's plain white, with only some very subtle grey accents. I'm fine with that, as the focus is on performance and comfort.

Any extra aesthetic fancies are likely to add to the weight, which isn't worth the sacrifice for this kind of mouse. As with most ultralight mice, you know what you're getting aesthetically, and it's minimal.

It has been revealed that this mouse uses the same software as the previous V2 Pro. What's noteworthy is the software is browser-based—there's no locally-installable app to use. That's mainly because you're expected to just set it and go, without returning to adjust things.

You can set up profiles to toggle between DPI using a mouse button combination, however. And the web software can be used offline if you install it as an app in your browser, so internet outages shouldn't cause any problems.

It has been revealed that the web hub is basic but gets the job done. The battery indicator isn't very precise, only showing a tiny icon and no percentage numbers, but that's my only complaint.

According to recent reports, the AimLabs integration is perfectly fine, too. Assuming you've got it installed on Steam, you can allow the web hub to boot it up for you from there, or boot it up yourself. Once in, you can navigate to PureVector and let it run you through the aim training to adjust your sensitivity in different sweep directions. It's intuitive, and the directional charts it demonstrates are clear enough.

Industry observers note that at $180/£160, the Sabre V3 Pro PureVector Ergo is an expensive mouse. It joins the likes of the G Pro X2/X3 Superstrike, Viper V4 Pro, DeathAdder V4 Pro, SteelSeries Rival Pro, and other high-end, competitive gaming mice.

Can it compete with these? In my opinion, not quite. These other gaming mice each have extra features and newly introduced technologies that go some way towards justifying the very high price tags. The Superstrikes have analogue clicks, the Viper V4 Pro has FrameSync, the Rival Pro has hot-swappable batteries and UWB connectivity.

In a recent development, the DeathAdder V4 Pro doesn't have anything too fancy like that, but is a very solid gaming mouse. I'd class the Sabre V3 Pro PureVector in this category, alongside the DeathAdder. That's because while the PureVector technology is indeed very upcoming, I haven't found it to have much of an impact, and so I'm left considering its merits as a general competitive gaming mouse, setting aside this new aim assist tech.

It has been revealed that there are merits to it that justify a price tag above $100: light weight, comfy ergonomic shape, optical clicks, responsive scroll wheel, great battery life. But not enough to justify $180—not without something extra, which PureVector promises but, in my case, fails to deliver. Unless, that is, you're set on getting a mouse as light as this one is that still has a sturdy shell.

According to recent reports, you could instead, for instance, go for something like the Mchose K7 V2 Ultra+ for about $90. Or a Pulsar mouse like the Pulsar X2 CrazyLight for $130, which sometimes drops to about $100 on sale.

If you fancy spending the extra to try it out for yourself and see if you can get the kinds of benefits the pros that Corsair highlights espouse, go for it. But for my money, I'd be opting for a cheaper lightweight mouse, or one with better build quality like the Viper V4 Pro.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

You may have recently read that CD Projekt Red's in-development Cyberpunk 2 may be trying to revive the original game's online ambitions. But, if you don't want to wait the many years it'll likely be before the Cyberpunk 2077 sequel arrives, then I've got good news for you: Cyberpunk 2077 multiplayer mod CyberMP is now out in open beta.

In a recent development, "After almost six years of development, countless reworks, and code rewrites, we're finally launching the public beta," the modders on the CyberMP Discord channel wrote (thanks RPS). "Anyone can jump in and play now - no invites or applications needed." The team notes, however, that this is "true beta", meaning "Crashes, desyncs, and server drops under heavy load are completely normal for now. That's exactly why we need testers.".

It has been revealed that alongside the potential shakiness, the devs say it's also possible the mod could ping your anti-virus software, since it "doesn't have a digital signature yet". Whilst the priorities for the team lie in "polishing the foundations" and "fixing crashes and stability", more features are eventually planned. But for now, they stress, "let's see how the project handles real player traffic!".

So, what exactly is it? CyberMP is a dedicated multiplayer modification for Cyberpunk 2077 that allows you and your friends to explore Night City together: drive vehicles, engage in combat, and play custom community-created game modes on high-tick dedicated servers. You need an official copy of the game to play it (obviously), and the mod is completely free to download. You can download the mod, and read a fair amount of how to get it working, what to expect from it, and how to troubleshoot any issues, over at its dedicated website.

If you're thinking 'Hang on, why does Cyberpunk 2077 multiplayer sound so familiar?', it's because the game was supposed to receive an official multiplayer mode after its original release. Thanks to its shaky launch, however, plans changed, and CD Projekt Red later confirmed that multiplayer would be a separate "triple-A release", but, eventually, that too was cancelled. The studio is still keen to honour the idea, though, and recently stated it's "focusing on bringing online into all of our franchises one day".

In a recent development, this isn't the first massive bit of news we've had about Cyberpunk 2077 mods this week. Just yesterday, a new mod called 'Torrent' added 3D rain, lightning storms, and tyre spray to Night City - all rendered and made lovely with a new lighting system that seems to play nicely with other weather mods that have been created for the game.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Stellar Blade: Blood Rain re-entered the limelight after its initial reveal late this summer with the arrival of a highly controversial music video full of generative AI content – a debacle that prompted Shift Up to reconsider its use of the contentious tech.

Although studio CEO Kim Hyung-tae initially defended the video as star Evie was originally "created from head to toe" by human developers, fans (unsurprisingly) were still not pleased. This led to Shift Up promising they're taking the community's concerns "seriously" – but still saying AI has "a lot of influence and impact on game development." So, where does the team stand now? And what role does generative tech play in the Stellar Blade sequel? Well, according to Kim, all of the Blood Rain music video backlash birthed a upcoming motto the devs now work by: "Handmade from start to finish." But, erm, it's crucial to note that this does not mean Shift Up isn't using AI at all. It's still there for intermediate tasks, as he tells Inven Global in a recent interview. Think texture weathering applications, reducing polygon counters for performance, testing lighting, and organization.

At the end of the process, though, human devs refine everything to ensure their work stands out against entirely AI-generated projects. But, again, AI is indeed in the picture. Kim states simply prioritizing "efficiency" and "productivity" during development isn't the way to go, however, emphasizing that Shift Up utilizes AI to bring a level of quality to games that's otherwise apparently not found – not to speed everything up for quicker releases.

He believes that games that do rely on AI for efficiency or productivity end up those that players regard as "slop" – you know, like the thousands that plagued Valve's latest Steam Next Fest and such. Working entirely without the worrisome tech is not really feasible anymore, though (or so Kim thinks, anyway), as it's used in everything in development from simple quality assurance to more in-depth debugging.

Recent findings suggest that so, to sum things up: Shift Up is evidently applying AI where it deems it appropriate, while still somehow prioritizing the whole "handmade" aspect of development. I'm not too sure this will calm the storm Blood Rain's music video spurred, but… Oh well.

The Weeknd turning up to play Stellar Blade: Blood Rain reveals the action RPG's appeal goes "beyond gaming" into "the wider cultural sphere," Shift Up says.

10 Hacks Every Reddit User Should Know

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (855 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • If you're looking for discussions, recommendations, or advice online, it's hard to avoid Reddit.
  • Industry observers note that reddit used to let everyone view your post and comment history, but in recent years, you can make your profile private.
  • Recent findings suggest that old Reddit lets you use the site's classic design, and I prefer it to the more modern UI.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you're looking for discussions, recommendations, or advice online, it's hard to avoid Reddit. From mainstream sports to niche crafts, it does seem that there's some kind of Reddit community for everyone. (And if there's not one, you can make one yourself.) If you're using Reddit, here are 10 hacks you should know about to improve your experience on the site.

Industry observers note that reddit used to let everyone view your post and comment history, but in recent years, you can make your profile private. You can hide your posts, comments, and the subreddits you're a part of. If you want to do this, click your profile icon once you've logged in to Reddit, and go to Settings > Profile. Alternatively, you can follow the direct link to Reddit's profile settings page. Click the drop-down menu next to Content & Activity, and select Hide all. You should also turn off Online Status on the same page to stop people from seeing when you're using Reddit.

Recent findings suggest that old Reddit lets you use the site's classic design, and I prefer it to the more modern UI. Old Reddit looks dated, but it doesn't have infinite scrolling, distracting animations, and a bunch of features designed to increase the time you spend on the platform. It's no wonder that Reddit is making it harder to access this version of the site. As long as it's around, you should switch to Old Reddit for a cleaner reading experience. You can do that by going to Reddit Settings > Preferences and enabling Default to Old Reddit. You can also visit old.reddit.com, though you'll need to sign in for access.

Many subreddits use custom themes that range from beautiful to borderline unusable. If you want a more consistent UI across the site, you should disable these custom subreddit styles. Go to Reddit Settings > Preferences and turn off Use community themes. If you're using Old Reddit, click the preferences button in the top-right corner, and under "display options," disable allow subreddits to show me custom themes.

Sources indicate that reddit's social features are useful if you have friends on the site, but in most cases, those features are annoying at best. If your post or comment goes viral, be prepared to deal with waves of weirdos who find it entertaining to send unsolicited advice or opinions. To keep all of this at bay, you should disable the site's social features. Go to Reddit Settings > Privacy, and turn off Allow people to follow you. On the same page, click Who can send you chat requests, and pick Nobody. You can also turn off Show up in search results to remove your profile from Google searches.

It has been revealed that A multireddit is a feed that reveals posts from a customized group of subreddits. You can think of it as a way to break out of Reddit's algorithms, and create your own Reddit feed. I use multireddits to follow all sports-related subs I'm interested in. I even have one for gaming, and one for fountain pens. It's a great way to create interest-specific feeds, and if you make them private, no one else can see them. To create one, click the Create custom feed button in the left pane in newly introduced Reddit. In the Old Reddit design, click the Create button in the left pane. Be sure to select the Private button to keep it from showing up for others. You can add as many subreddits as you like to the list, and bookmark the feed to access it whenever you wish to.

If you want to reduce Reddit's tracking, you should turn off ad personalization. Go to Reddit Settings > Privacy, and turn off Personalize ads. To block Reddit's ads altogether, you can use any ad blocker you like. I recommend uBlock Origin, which is one of the best ad blockers you can install, though most can hide Reddit's ads on desktop. On mobile, you can try using AdGuard or Wipr to hide in-app ads in Reddit.

Sources indicate that reddit has recently adopted an Instagram-like experience for its feeds. It removed the ability to sort posts by new, controversial, best, etc., and instead offers "For You" and "Following." If you dislike this change, you can bypass it. I use Reddit on mobile Safari, and I recommend an extension called Sink It for Reddit. It can automatically redirect you to Old Reddit, and there's a feature that optimizes it for mobile, which brings back the old sorting options. You can also use third-party apps such as RedReader for Android, or RDX for Reddit on an iPhone or iPad to restore the old sorting options for Reddit posts.

It has been revealed that after all these years, Reddit's built-in search still leaves something to be desired—at least, on the surface. To find posts on Reddit faster, use search filters on the site. For instance, adding "title:" to your search will limit the results to post titles, and boolean operators such as AND, OR, and NOT also work for advanced searches on the site.
